This did not involve the type of constant or close to full-time keyboarding activity for which the Tribunal has in the past granted entitlement for epicondylitis.

Further, there was evidence of vasospastic changes in the worker's feet, which were, in fact, more marked than in her hands. If the changes were related to use of the buffer-polisher, the changes would have been more marked in her hands.

The reconsideration requests made on behalf of the worker have included allegations of bias, procedural irregularities and other improprieties against the panel that was previously seized of this matter before the present Panel's involvement.
The worker's application for reconsideration of Decision No. 923/03I was denied. There was no significant error in the process or content of the decision.

The reconsideration requests made on behalf of the worker have included allegations of bias, procedural irregularities and other improprieties against the panel that was previously seized of this matter before the present Panel's involvement.

The worker's application for reconsideration of Decisions No. 923/03I, 923/03IR, 923/03IR2 and 923/03IR3 was denied. The worker was essentially making the same arguments regarding bias and conflict of interest that he made in the previous reconsideration applications. The worker submitted evidence from his family doctor indicating that the worker reported increased anxiety as a result of a teleconference and the conduct of the vice-chair in that proceeding. The Panel found that the conduct of the vice-chair was appropriate and that the worker was provided with an opportunity to voice his issues calmly, as recommended by his doctor.
